transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Lee. Well... I suppose it's my sleep. It's just... become completely unmoored lately. 

For a while, I'd be up after just two or three hours, and I'd be... drafting plans, feeling entirely ready to go. But now... I just lie awake before dawn. My stomach gets tight, and there's just... no sense of rest anymore. So... I suppose that's why I'm here.

During that earlier time when you were only sleeping two or three hours but felt ready to go, how would you describe your mood and energy during the day—were you feeling unusually upbeat, confident, or full of energy?

Well... yes, I suppose you could say that. I felt... very optimistic. Almost brilliantly so, for a few weeks. It just seemed like... any obstacle was trivial. I had a lot of energy. 

But... I didn't have much patience. If anyone questioned my plans or... got in my way, I'm afraid I snapped at them. It just felt like they were trying to sabotage things, and I was the only one making any sense.
You mentioned feeling unusually optimistic and energetic for a few weeks—can you tell me exactly how many days in a row that elevated mood and energy lasted before it changed?
I... I couldn't give you an exact number. I didn't exactly mark it on a calendar or anything like that. It was just... a period of time. A few weeks, as I said. I really don't know beyond that.
During those few weeks of feeling so energetic and optimistic, did family, friends, or coworkers notice a clear change in your behavior, or did it cause any problems at work or in your relationships?

Yes... I suppose people noticed. My wife, certainly. She... well, she's had to take over all the finances recently. And she insists on staying close by... says it's for my safety, though I... I don't know. 

As for the rest... I haven't been going to my usual commitments. The museum board, the arts council... I just stopped showing up. And I haven't really been seeing friends either. So... yes, it's caused some changes.
You mentioned lying awake before dawn with a tight stomach and no sense of rest—how long has this current low, unrested feeling been going on, day after day?

I suppose... it's been quite a while now. Ever since all those plans I had just... fell apart. 

It's been... maybe nine months? Nine months of this... low feeling. Just wanting to pull away from everything. The guilt... it just sits there. Day after day.
During this past nine months of low mood, have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or ending your life, or experienced any unusual beliefs or perceptions—like hearing things others don't?

I haven't heard or seen anything unusual, no. But... as for the other part... 

It's difficult to talk about. There are mornings when I... well, when I think it would just be a relief if I simply did not wake up. It's not something I want to dwell on. But I did... I frightened myself enough recently that I told my wife she probably shouldn't leave me alone. That's... that's all I really want to say about that.
